question: What percentage of total hospital waste is generally made up of non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: The majority of hospital waste is general refuse that poses no direct health risk and can be handled like normal household trash. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why must a nurse sort and classify healthcare waste right at the bedside?

options.A: It prevents hazardous items from mixing with safe trash and reducing risks.
options.B: It makes the waste room look neat and tidy for incoming visitors.
options.C: It ensures that kitchen scraps are safely sterilized before recycling.
options.D: It helps the hospital save money on buying heavy-duty office paper.

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right away stops dangerous things like used needles from ending up in normal trash bags where they could easily prick and injure anyone handling them. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h1)

question: What type of waste belongs inside a puncture-resistant safety box?
explanation: Safety boxes are specially designed to safely contain sharp objects like needles and blades without letting them pierce through. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h2)

question: You just finished dressing a patient's wound with blood-stained gauze. Which bin should this gauze go into?
explanation: Well done! Blood-soaked materials are considered infectious waste, so they always go into the yellow bin or bag for safe, specialized treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h2)

question: How full should a medical waste bag be before you tie it up and take it away?
explanation: You got it! Stopping at three-quarters full leaves you enough space to securely tie the bag shut without risking nasty tears or accidental punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which of these actions is a major safety violation when storing medical waste in a hospital?

options.A: Locking the storage room door at night
options.D: Leaving bags in public hospital corridors

explanation: Exactly right! Medical waste should never sit in public hallways where patients, visitors, or staff could trip over, knock over, or tear the bags. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h3)

question: What does an autoclave primarily use to sterilize infectious medical waste?
explanation: Autoclaves rely on pressurized steam to reach temperatures high enough to destroy bacteria, viruses, and spores. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h4)

question: What happens to infectious soft waste after it successfully goes through an autoclave cycle?

options.A: It becomes radioactive and needs special deep burial.
options.B: It instantly turns into liquid that pours down the drain.
options.C: It is sterilized and can often be handled like general waste.
options.D: It must still be burned in an open outdoor pit.

explanation: You're doing great! Once an autoclave kills all the infectious germs, the treated waste is safe and no longer poses a biological hazard. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which of these materials must always be disposed of through incineration?
explanation: Correct! Anatomical waste requires complete thermal destruction via incineration for both sanitary safety and cultural respect. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the clay and plastic lining inside a sanitary landfill?

options.A: To keep the landfill smelling fresh for nearby communities
options.B: To help burn the buried waste faster using natural ground heat
options.C: To attract earthworms that break down plastic materials
options.D: To prevent toxic liquid leachate from reaching underground water

explanation: Engineered liners act as a barrier to stop harmful chemicals and liquids from polluting local groundwater sources. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do after accidentally getting a needle stick injury?

options.A: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.B: Wash the wound immediately with soap and running water
options.C: Cover the tiny puncture mark with heavy makeup
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow joint

explanation: Spot on! Washing the site right away with soap and water helps wash away or reduce any germs that entered through the broken skin. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h6)

question: You are cleaning a utility room that has broken glass and used syringes. Which protective gear do you need most?

options.A: An ordinary cloth mask and rubber slippers
options.B: Heavy utility gloves and protective eyewear
options.C: Soft examination gloves and plastic shoes
options.D: A sterile white gown and a surgical cap

explanation: You got it! Thick utility gloves protect your hands from cuts and punctures, while eyewear keeps any accidental splashes of dirty fluids out of your eyes. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards and regulations?
explanation: Correct! NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) keeps an eye on environmental compliance and pollution control across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h7)

question: What is a major challenge many healthcare facilities in Nigeria face when trying to dispose of waste?

options.A: Having too many modern autoclaves than needed
options.B: Excessive funding for environmental protection programs
options.C: Unreliable electricity supply that halts incinerator operations
options.D: Lack of any medical waste being generated in wards

explanation: Spot on! Frequent power cuts can shut down electrical incinerators and big sterilization machines, making safe waste management a real daily struggle. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h7)
